{{Short description|Theorem}}
In [[mathematics]], '''Noether's theorem on rationality for surfaces''' is a classical result of [[Max Noether]] on complex [[algebraic surface]]s, giving a criterion for a [[rational surface]]. Let ''S'' be an algebraic surface that is [[Algebraic curve#Singularities|non-singular]] and projective. Suppose there is a morphism φ from ''S'' to the [[projective line]], with ''general fibre'' also a projective line. Then the theorem states that ''S'' is rational.<ref>{{cite journal | doi=10.1007/BF01366911 | volume=11 | title=The castelnuovo criterion of rationality | year=1972 | journal=Mathematical Notes of the Academy of Sciences of the USSR | pages=20–23 | last1 = Kurke | first1 = G.}}</ref>
